full.body:
Merons

The supposed transformation of supposed "neutrons" into supposed "protons" is a phenomenon that physicists say is widely observed in the processes of "nuclear fission" or the natural decay of so-called "radioisotopes". In this process, according to conventional atomic physics, there is a release of energy, and as the supposed "neutrons" are more massive than the supposed "protons", part of their "mass" would be "converted" into "energy" and, consequently, they would be "transmuted" into those "protons". This is because, according to physicists, "matter" could be completely "converted" into energy, and vice versa.

However, according to the logical principles of the TUIDG Meronic Model, the idea of ​​"energy" is not that of an "indefinite fragmentation" of "matter", as this does not make sense. So that such "energy" is nothing more than the Apparent Motion of "oscillation/vibration" of the geometric structure of the Compalphas, which are the constituents of the Merons, and which are subject, for example, to the internal processes of a Uranium 235 bar in the fission process. In this deconstruction process, a Metalpha Meron can be interpreted as a "thermal neutron", which, disconnected from its original structure, is expelled with a lot of "kinetic energy", with intense rotation, and which, when passing through other types of Merons, or among their similar ones (in the original structure or outside it), does not interact promptly, until it loses part of this rotation, and is "geometrically absorbed" by these structures, causing or not their rupture.

The Structural (or Matrix) Number

The determination of the number of complete (or closed) cuboctahedral structures is given as a function of the number of Compalphas that constitute the Merons, and can be obtained by the formula Ne = (Nc − T) / K, where K = 9 and T = 3:

Ne represents the Structural Number, that is, the number of cuboctahedral structures in each Meron type;

Nc represents the Component Number, which is the total number of Compalphas in each Meron type;

K represents the Meronic Growth Constant, which increases in number by 9 Compalphas units with each closure of new Cuboctahedral structures;

T represents the Alpha Triad: the three Compalphas shared in the interaction between any two Cuboctahedra in the Meron structure.

So, knowing the value of the “mass” of the Meron, that is, how many times a certain Meron is “heavier” than another, we can determine how many Cuboctahedra this Meron has, and based on this number, what its spatial shape is. And knowing the shapes of the Meronic structures, we can assemble or pre-fabricate, through virtual models, all types of molecules, according to each physical-chemical need.

The Component Number

Through the Component Number, we can determine the number of Compalphas that a certain type of Meron has through its number of Cuboctahedra. This number is taken from the formula Nc = Ne × K + T, where K = 9 and T = 3:

Nc represents the Component Number

Ne represents the Structural Number

K represents the Meronic Growth Constant

T represents the Common Triad of Interaction

Knowing how many Compalphas there are in each type of Meron, we can make a much more precise relationship between the “masses” of these different types of Merons. For example, consider the Meron Dodecalpha (carbon 12) which has 111 Compalphas distributed and forming its 12 Cuboctahedra and the Meron Octalpha (Lithium 8), with its 75 Compalphas distributed and forming its 8 Cuboctahedra. So, we have: 111/75 = 1.48, this is the ratio between the “masses” of the two types of Merons.

According to the TUIDG Meronic Model, the form of growth of Merons (atoms), therefore, the increase in their mass, is due to the addition of Cuboctahedra to a pre-existing structure. Each Cuboctahedron is made up of 12 Compalphas, but as in each addition (or fusion) of a new cube, an Alpha Triad is eliminated from the structure, in the sum of two cubes, the total number (mass) of Compalphas is not 24 as we might think, but is given by the formula Nc = Ne × K + T, which gives:

Ne = 2 Cubes;

K = 9 Compalphas (K is the growth constant);

T = 3 Compalphas (1 Alpha Triad).

So, 2.9 + 3 = 21.
